title: Pass, fail or incomplete: contrast and heading checks
purpose: See how an automated accessibility check decides pass, fail or incomplete for color contrast and heading order, and what it leaves for a person.
sequence_reason: Each result depends on a measured value and a threshold, so the walkthrough builds the rule one part at a time and pauses for predictions.
summary: An accessibility scan gives three answers: pass, fail or incomplete. The contrast ratio is (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05). Normal text needs at least 4.5:1, large text at least 3:1. Gray #767676 on white scores 4.54 and passes; #777777 scores 4.47 and fails, because axe rounds down. A background image, an overlapping element, one-character text or an empty input gives incomplete. Heading order fails when a heading is more than one level deeper than the one before it. A person still judges text on images, heading meaning, and keyboard and screen reader use.
explanation: A rule decides only what it can measure. When it cannot see the real colors or the previous heading, it answers incomplete instead of guessing, and a person reviews it.

learning_check.question: Gray #777777 normal-size text on white measures 4.48:1. What does the contrast check report, and why?
learning_check.answer: Fail. The ratio is rounded down to 4.47, which is below the 4.5:1 that normal text needs.

scenes.heading: One scan, three answers
scenes.narration: One accessibility scan gives three answers: pass, fail, or incomplete. Incomplete means the tool cannot decide, so a person must review it.

scenes.heading: The contrast ratio
scenes.narration: The contrast ratio compares two colors. L1 is the relative luminance of the lighter color, and L2 is the luminance of the darker color.

terms.note: relative luminance of the lighter color
relative luminance of the darker color
a fixed constant added to both luminances

scenes.heading: Two thresholds
scenes.narration: Normal text needs a ratio of at least 4.5 to 1. Large text, 18 point or 14 point bold, needs at least 3 to 1.

left.label: Normal text
items: Below 18 pt, or below 14 pt bold

visual.verdict: Larger text may use lower contrast.

scenes.heading: No rounding up
scenes.narration: Gray 767676 on white scores 4.54 and passes. Gray 777777 scores 4.47 and fails. Axe rounds down, so 4.47 never shows as 4.5.

scenes.heading: When the tool cannot tell
scenes.narration: Some cases return incomplete: text on a background image, an overlapping element, one-character text, or an empty input field.

scenes.heading: Heading order
scenes.narration: Heading order checks each heading against the one before it. After h2, an h4 skips a level and fails. Change it to h3, and it passes.

scenes.heading: What rules cannot judge
scenes.narration: A rule decides plain color contrast and skipped heading levels. A person judges text on images, heading meaning, and keyboard and screen reader use.

visual.verdict: Zero violations does not mean accessible.
